key_idea: A transcendental λ with dimension drop is approximated superexponentially well by algebraic ξ that also have dimension drop and bounded Mahler measure. At the scale |λ−ξ| = (5M)^{-n}, Theorem 6 then supplies a small polynomial at λ. This contradicts a Liouville-type lower bound at ξ, transferred to λ through transversality and a derivative bound.
reason: The argument is short and conceptually clean once the heavy theorems are in hand. Its decisive move, matching the approximation scale to the scale at which exponentially small polynomials must exist, makes the contradiction feel forced. It loses some elegance because it depends on large black boxes (Theorems 6, 8, 9 and 11) and on a case split with a trimmed measure to handle λ>2^{-2/3}, which the author admits could be avoided.
recognized: Varjú, 'On the dimension of Bernoulli convolutions for all transcendental parameters' (Annals of Math. 2019)
